items.title: Can UPS Keep Improving Margins as Network Savings Reach $3 Billion?
items.summary: UPS is targeting about $3 billion in 2026 network savings as stronger pricing, higher cash flow and cost cuts support margins despite weaker package volumes.

items.title: 'We're Not Big Brother': Flock CEO Unveils New Privacy Guardrails After Backlash
items.summary: Flock Safety plans to establish new guardrails for its technology following backlash over allegations that its automated license plate readers are being misused and enabling mass surveillance.

items.title: FedEx and others announce layoffs in Southern California
items.summary: More than 500 people have lost jobs at FedEx, Staples and LAZ Parking; two facilities in Palm Springs and Victorville will close.

items.title: Nike, FedEx Reap Billions From Tariff Refunds: Who Actually Gets To Keep Them?
items.summary: Nike benefits from nearly $1 billion in tariff refunds, while FedEx plans to return its $800 million refund to customers.

items.title: A surprise credit after an overseas purchase: The tariff refunds now flowing through shippers
items.summary: Shippers including FedEx and UPS that acted as customs brokers for imported packages and received tariff refunds from the U.S. government have started to pass on those refunds to the customers that originally paid the tariffs.  The refunds to consumers are the last step in a monthslong process that kicked off in February when the Supreme Court struck down sweeping tariffs implemented by President Donald Trumpin March 2025 under the 1977 International Emergency Economic Powers Act on goods from almost every country.  The court ordered the government to return the tariffs it collected.

items.title: Tariff Refunds Are Here—and Turbocharging Earnings
items.summary: Apple, Nike and FedEx are just some of the companies that are recovering big sums relatively quickly.
